== Biography ==
Samuel was born about 1846.<ref>Based on age 54 at 1901 census.</ref> He was the son of [[Glasgow-1701|James Glasgow]] and lived at Killycurragh as of 1869.

On 28 Sep 1869 at 2nd Moneymore Meeting House (Presbyterian), he married Catherine Bole of Oritor, daughter of Andrew Bole, farmer. Attended by [[Henry-6237|Silas Weir Henry]] and Thomas Smyth.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/bc471f3065347 Samuel Glasgow, Catherine Bole, 1869, Magherafelt] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

He and son Fred attend the funeral of his sister [[Glasgow-1707|Nancy Glasgow (abt.1836-1896)]].

As of 1901, 4 of their children live at Newtownards, County Down.
<ref>[https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#id=5133427 1901 Ireland census] - Residents of a house 29 in High Street (Newtownards Urban, Down). Robert James(24), Frederick Charles(30, brother), Thomas John (18, brother), Margaret Jane(21, sister), Harold Agnew(4, son), Sara Perter(26, visitor).</ref>

He passed away 1 September 1919 at Killycurragh, age 73, due to heart disease, and is buried at Cookstown New Cemetery with wife Catherine, and son Allen and his wife.
<ref>{{FindAGrave|169851195}}</ref>
<ref>[[Space:Forthill Cemetery, Cookstown, Tyrone]] - OP/E/58. The cemetery site does not give his middle name, but the headstone says "S.J." (I have seen a photo)</ref>
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/8eaa7e3657103 Samuel Glasgow, 1919, Cookstown, 73] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths. Informant: Allen Glasgow, son.</ref>
A marriage for Sam Glasgow and Bole was registered on 28 September 1869 in the Cookstown district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 28 September 1869, Cookstown district, M/1869/L1/1122/2/7.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1701]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Samuel's 1869 marriage account names James and places him at Killycurragh. Nancy's funeral calls him brother, joining him to the securely identified James junior family.

Selected Glasgow-1701 fatherhood of Glasgow-1722; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Read original 1869 marriage and Nancy's funeral wording together.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/bc471f3065347 Samuel Glasgow, Catherine Bole, 1869, Magherafelt (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/bc471f3065347) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
